market.worldSizeUSD_B_range: Biometric identity verification market: $8.88B (2025) to $17.81B by 2030, CAGR 14.9%. Broader biometric systems market: ~$53.22B (2025) to $95.14B by 2030, CAGR ~12.3%.
globalCompetitors: Thales (France, biometrics-segment revenue not separately disclosed)
market.domesticSlice: India biometrics market: $2.8B (2024) to $7.36B by 2033, CAGR 11.33%, anchored by Aadhaar (1.2B+ enrolled, ~95% of population) and UIDAI's mandatory 'Registered Device' certification regime for authentication hardware

structureFacts: UIDAI mandates STQC L1/FBI-PIV certified 'Registered Devices' for Aadhaar authentication — a hard regulatory gate on the domestic device market, not just a quality signal
e-KYC substantially lowers verification cost vs paper-based methods, a structural driver behind BFSI/telecom biometric adoption
Global demand is also driven by border-security and fraud-prevention mandates outside India

adoptionStructure.note: Not a seasonal-repurchase category like seeds; demand is procurement-cycle driven (government tenders, BFSI onboarding volumes) rather than a fixed replacement rate

drivers: UIDAI-mandated device registration/certification (STQC L1, FBI PIV) — a hard gate, not optional
cost and field-durability for rural/handheld enrollment use cases
customerValue.strongestPredictor: regulatory certification (UIDAI Registered Device status) — without it, a device cannot legally serve the Aadhaar-linked market at all

steps: brand & position on certification + liveness performance
plan production against government/enterprise order cycles
sell direct to government/enterprise or via reseller/integrator channel
demand arises (government tender or BFSI/telecom KYC need)
